descriptionChirho: Active giving of counsel or advice to another person, corresponding to Arabic أَشَارَ (ashara) 'to advise' and Korean 조언하다 (jo-eon-hada) 'to counsel'.

Purposing, planning, or determining a course of action, often of God's sovereign decree, corresponding to Arabic قَصَدَ/قَضَى (qasada/qadaa) 'to intend/determine' and Korean 계획하다 (gyehoek-hada) 'to plan'; includes negative scheming in context.

Substantivized Qal active participle denoting a counselor or adviser as an office or role, corresponding to Arabic مُشِير (mushir) 'counselor' and Korean 모사 (mosa) 'counselor'; Swahili mshauri/washauri confirms agentive derivation.

Reciprocal or reflexive deliberation, consulting together or taking counsel with others, corresponding to Arabic تَشَاوَرَ/اِسْتَشَارَ (tashawara/istashara) 'to consult mutually' and Korean 의논하다 (uinon-hada) 'to discuss'; includes Niphal perfects, imperfects, participles, and the sole Hitpael occurrence.

Qal passive participle denoting that which has been determined or decreed, corresponding to Arabic الْمَقْصُودُ (al-maqsud) 'the intended/purposed thing' and Korean 계획된 (gyehoek-doen) 'that which is planned'.
